 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Last week, Houston Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter made a play on the football late in the fourth quarter against the Cleveland Browns . The hit was called a penalty, tacking on extra yards while keeping the drive alive for Cleveland amid a 27-24 victory.
 But something happened during the game that had fans wonder about Lassiter's long-term status. Earlier this week, he appeared on the injury report with a wrist strain and did not practice on Tuesday.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With it being a short week, there's little time to recover. But the Texans are in win-now mode for the remainder of the regular season, starting on Thursday night against the Indianapolis Colts on Amazon Prime, meaning anyone who is healthy needs to play, including the former Pro Bowl cornerback.
 So, will Lassiter be good to go for Thursday night's action at Reliant Stadium?
 Kamari Lassiter injury update: Will the CB play in Week 11?
 Lassiter did practice on Wednesday, so it could have been a one-day stinger that limited his reps. On the final injury report, nothing appeared next to his name, meaning that barring a last-second injury, he should be cleared to return to the field for Week 11's matchup against the Colts on Thursday Night Football.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A second-round pick out of Georgia and one of the top cover cornerbacks last season, Lassiter has dealt with his fair share of struggles in coverage this fall. While he ranks second in tackles with 52 stops, Lassiter has also allowed four touchdowns in coverage. He's only broken up 10 passes and has yet to record an inteception.
 Perhaps the biggest fault on the docket is the penalties. In every game started this season, Lassiter has been flagged at least once for a play, usually a holding or pass interference call.
